gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Epson PowerLite 1781W has no Miracast. Epson gives Miracast screen mirroring only to the PowerLite 1785W and 1795F. A presenter can't use Windows' built-in Cast to send their screen to the 1781W without a cable. Wireless projection needs Epson's iProjection app, and on macOS 10.15 to 14 iProjection shows a black desktop until the app gets Screen Recording permission.
standout_why: I compared against picks.beecommercer.com (cited), projectorverdict.com and geeksalad.org. Beecommercer already says the CO-FH02's single HDMI is taken by its streaming player and that the Capsule 3 Laser's USB-C isn't a verified laptop video input. It does not cover the 1781W at all. Projectorverdict doesn't name the 1781W and never mentions Miracast, iProjection or USB plug-and-play video. Geeksalad mentions Miracast only for the Epson EX9270 and also leaves out the 1781W. I tried three times to read rottenwifi.com (cited) and every attempt timed out, so I can't rule out that it covers this. techradar.com returned only its title.
decides: This confirms the 1781W as the most flexible for connections of the three Epsons ChatGPT showed. It has HDMI with MHL, VGA, composite and a USB Type-B port for plug-and-play USB projection. The two EpiqVision Flex models list only a built-in HDMI port on their Epson pages. The catch is wireless. A visiting presenter can't use Windows' built-in Cast; they need the iProjection app, and a Mac also needs Screen Recording permission granted. If the shopper wants app-free wireless from Windows or Android, Epson's own document points to the PowerLite 1785W or 1795F instead.

findings.label: Miracast screen mirroring
findings.value: Not on the 1781W. Epson lists 'Miracast screen mirroring for laptops and mobile devices' only for the PowerLite 1785W and 1795F
findings.source_title: Epson PowerLite 1780W/1781W/1785W/1795F User's Guide: Your projector includes these special features
findings.note: This feature list covers four models. The Miracast bullet names 1785W/1795F, and the same list also limits Gesture Presenter to those two models.

findings.label: Wireless projection path
findings.value: Wireless network projection, and projection from iOS or Android devices using the free Epson iProjection app. The list also includes plug-and-play USB projection.
findings.source_title: Epson PowerLite 1780W/1781W/1785W/1795F User's Guide: Your projector includes these special features
findings.note: These connectivity bullets carry no model restriction on the page.

findings.label: Wired inputs
findings.value: 1× HDMI (supports MHL), 1× D-sub 15-pin (VGA), 1× RCA composite, 1× USB Type B ('USB Plug 'n Play'), 1× USB Type A (PC-free)
findings.note: Taken from the Interfaces section of the product page. The page also says 'compatible with PC and Mac computers' and that it 'Includes a high-speed LAN module for wireless connectivity'. A generic footnote on the same page tells buyers to check whether a wireless module is sold separately, so the page contradicts itself here.

findings.label: USB Display (video over the USB cable) OS support
findings.source_title: Epson support FAQ, PowerLite 1781W: How do I install the USB Display software on my computer?
findings.note: Epson's answer reads: 'The software supports Mac and Windows only.' It says to get the latest version from the Downloads tab on the projector's support page. The FAQ gives no specific OS versions.

findings.label: iProjection on Mac
findings.value: On macOS 10.15.x, 11, 12, 13 and 14, iProjection shows a black desktop unless Epson iProjection is granted Screen Recording access in Privacy settings
findings.source_title: Epson support FAQ, PowerLite 1781W: black desktop when projecting with Epson iProjection on macOS
findings.note: Epson's fix is System Settings > Privacy > Screen Recording > check Epson iProjection. If iProjection is missing from that list, reinstall it.

findings.label: Price, brightness, resolution, weight (Epson US store)
findings.value: $899.99; 3,200 lm color and white; WXGA 1280 × 800; 4.0 lb
findings.note: ChatGPT's card showed $983.83 from a retailer it did not name, so Epson's own store is $83.84 cheaper.

findings.label: Casting and streaming
findings.value: Android TV and Chromecast included; casting from Android and Apple devices 'may require additional software'; streaming player powered by an included Mini-USB cable; $499.99
findings.source_title: Epson EpiqVision Flex CO-FH02 Full HD 1080p Smart Portable Projector (V11HA85020)
findings.note: Footnote 5 sends readers to Google for current device and OS support. Android TV needs Wi-Fi of 5 Mbps or faster. The page doesn't mention AirPlay or Miracast.

findings.label: Inputs and price
findings.value: A 'built-in HDMI port' is the only input the page names; $399.99
findings.source_title: Epson EpiqVision Flex CO-W01 Portable Projector (V11HA86020)
findings.note: The full spec table sits in a separate PDF that I didn't open, so I'm not claiming a port count.

findings.label: iPhone/iPad mirroring
findings.value: No AirPlay out of the box. You must first install the Nebula Cast app from Google Play on the projector. DRM content (Netflix, Disney+, Hulu, MAX, Prime Video) cannot be mirrored or cast via AirPlay.
findings.source_title: How do I mirror or stream video from iOS devices to Capsule 3 Laser? (Anker/Nebula support)
findings.note: The phone and projector must be on the same network. For a Mac, the article says DRM video needs an HDMI cable.

unsourced: HDMI port count, weight and a VGA yes/no for the CO-FH02 and CO-W01: Epson's product pages put these in spec PDFs that I didn't open, so I left them out.

Whether the Capsule 3 Laser's USB-C port carries video: Nebula's 'What ports does Capsule 3 Laser have?' page and its Capsule 3 Laser FAQ both returned 404, and I found no maker document saying either way.

Whether the 1781W's USB Display supports macOS 15 or later: Epson's 1781W FAQ names only Mac and Windows, and the macOS 10.15 to 14 range comes from the iProjection FAQ. The only newer-macOS note I found was a search result about a different Epson model (E24), which I didn't open.

Whether the 1781W's wireless LAN module is built in or sold separately: the product page says it's included, but a generic footnote on the same page says some models need it bought separately, and I didn't open the 1781W manual to settle it.
rottenwifi.com (cited by ChatGPT): the page timed out on all three fetch attempts, so I couldn't check whether it already covers the 1781W's missing Miracast.
